question: What are the blessings of Masjid al-Aqsa?
answer:
Now, the blessings of Aqsa are very, very many. Overall, the blessings are very, very many. And the fact of the matter is that I have given longer lectures, and others have given many lectures, about the blessings of Aqsa. In fact, many are the scholars that have even written entire treatises and entire books of hadith in which they have compiled the blessings of al-Aqsa. And especially those scholars that used to live in al-Aqsa: there was a great family, the al-Maqdisi family. Al-Maqdisi because they lived in the Muqaddas land. So of the names of Aqsa is al-Ard al-Muqaddas, the holy land. This is in the Qur'an: al-Ard al-Muqaddas, the holy land.

And there was a group of scholars of a great family that lived there for many centuries. There are at least half a dozen al-Maqdisis, al-Maqadisa, and to this day their descendants are there. In fact, one famous al-Maqdisi actually wrote one of the most famous books and compilations of hadith about the blessings of Masjid al-Aqsa.

So there are many, many blessings of Masjid al-Aqsa. And of course, the greatest blessing for us is that it is the land of the prophets and the land of the first qiblah, the area that our Prophet ﷺ would face for 14, 15 years of his life. The entire Meccan seerah, the phase of the Meccan time frame, the qiblah was Bayt al-Maqdis, Masjid al-Aqsa. And then the first few months of migrating to Medina, it was also Masjid al-Aqsa. And then the Prophet ﷺ turned to face Mecca.

And the fact that he traveled there and prayed: he ﷺ physically visited al-Aqsa. And it is the only place on earth where all the prophets simultaneously gathered and prayed two raka'ah, as we learn in the books of seerah. The only place on earth; no other place has been chosen by Allah where all the prophets gathered.

And Allah 'azza wa jall mentions that it is blessed, and the land around it is blessed, and that it is blessed for all of mankind. The verse in the Qur'an says: this is a land that We have blessed for all nations. And to this day, Muslims, Christians and Jews (and they are the majority of mankind; these three religions put together are more than 50% of mankind), all of these groups of mankind consider Jerusalem to be holy. No other land is considered to be holy by so many people. No other land on earth is considered to be blessed and holy by so many people as al-Aqsa.

And the question of how many prayers more it is blessed: this is something that many scholars have differed over, because what we actually have is a number of opinions about how many times blessed it is. And we do have a number of hadith that bless al-Aqsa generically. For example, there is a hadith in Sunan an-Nasa'i in which our Prophet ﷺ said that when Sulayman ibn Dawud finished building Bayt al-Maqdis, he asked Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala for three blessings:

1. That his verdict would be correct: that the judgment Sulayman chooses would be the judgment of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. So whenever he gave a judgment, whenever he made a decree, it would be the correct decree.
2. A kingdom the likes of which no one after him would ever have.
3. That no one comes to this masjid wanting to pray in it except that all of his sins shall be forgiven when he comes and prays in Masjid al-Aqsa.

And the Prophet ﷺ said: for sure he was given the first two, and I'm hopeful, I'm optimistic, that he was given the last one as well. This is a hadith in the Sunan of Imam an-Nasa'i. So our Prophet ﷺ said that he asked for three things, the last one being that whoever prays in Masjid al-Aqsa shall have all of his sins forgiven.

And we also have a number of traditions in Ibn Majah and others (and some of these have been disputed in their chains, but the concept is there) that even if you cannot pray in Masjid al-Aqsa, at least give some oil to Masjid al-Aqsa to light the lanterns, to give some light to Masjid al-Aqsa. So the point is that we should try our best to service Masjid al-Aqsa. If we are told to give some oil so that the lanterns can have some oil, then what do you think about defending that area in which the lights are? If we're told to even light the place up, how much more so to defend the area with all that we have. So we have a number of traditions that praise Masjid al-Aqsa.
